title: File upload with size and type checks
description: Server file uploads with a streaming size limit (413 without buffering the rest), magic-byte type detection, an allowlist that must agree with the extension and declared type, sanitized names and random storage keys, a browser preflight, per-tenant authorization and atomic quota, quarantine until an injected scanner marks files clean, and safe attachment serving.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, Web Crypto randomUUID, TextEncoder/TextDecoder, ReadableStream and the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
client.ts and policy.ts are browser-safe (no Node APIs) and run in any modern browser for the upload preflight; core.ts, http.ts and the stores are server-only.
The upload body is the raw file (fetch PUT/POST with the File as body), not multipart/form-data.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: Set policy.maxBytes and policy.allow (default png, jpeg, gif, webp, pdf); use the same policy object in preflight on the client and createFileUploads on the server.
Implement BlobStore (put/get/delete) over your object storage (S3, R2, GCS, disk) keyed by the random storageKey; MemoryBlobStore is for tests.

On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlUploadMetadataStore with your query executor; elsewhere implement UploadMetadataStore with a single conditional quota reservation and conditional status change and delete.
Pass authorize(user, tenantId, action) for upload, read and delete, and quotaBytes as a number or per-tenant function.

Pass scanner(bytes, record) backed by your antivirus (for example a ClamAV daemon or a scanning service) and call scanPending() from a background job (or scan(id) from a queue worker), or call recordScanResult(id, verdict) from your own pipeline. No antivirus engine is included.

Match your spec with options instead of wrapper code: policy.extensions (accepted extensions per type), policy.filenameControls ("remove"), policy.invalidFilenames ("reject" → invalid-name), checkDeclaredType: false (ignore the client's Content-Type on the server), lengthMismatch ("too-large") and scanLeaseMs.
Mount createFileUploadHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins and an authenticate(request) that reads your session; also cap the request body size at your proxy or platform.
limitations: No antivirus or malware engine is included; scanning is an injected hook, and without a scanner (or recordScanResult) every upload stays quarantined and is never served.
Accepted bytes are buffered in memory up to policy.maxBytes before they reach the BlobStore; it does not stream to object storage or support resumable or multipart/form-data uploads.
A single oversized chunk delivered by the runtime is already in memory when it is counted; cap request bodies at the proxy or platform too.

Without Content-Length the rest of maxBytes is reserved while it fits the quota, else quota is reserved chunk by chunk; near a full quota, several concurrent streamed uploads can each be cut off partway (none exceeds the quota). Send Content-Length to reserve exactly up front.

Type detection covers png, jpeg, gif, webp, pdf, zip and a UTF-8 plain-text heuristic (plus svg/html recognition to refuse them); it does not validate the whole file structure, so re-encode images if you render them.
zip is detected as a container only; docx, xlsx and other zip-based formats are refused rather than identified.
If release or blob deletion fails after a metadata delete, quota or an orphaned blob may need reconciliation by a scheduled job.
The in-memory stores are single-process; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which runs as a single connection, not under real multi-connection contention.
Production storage, antivirus accuracy, proxy body limits and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: routes: POST {prefix}/tenants/{tenantId}/files?filename= (raw bytes, not multipart), GET|DELETE {prefix}/files/{id}
default allowlist png, jpeg, gif, webp, pdf; type sniffed from bytes; mismatch → 415
new files stay quarantined until a claimed scan is clean; quarantined download → 409, infected → 410
too-large and quota-exceeded → 413; invalid-name → 400; downloads always use Content-Disposition: attachment

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/file-uploads.test.mjs tests/file-uploads-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: a declared Content-Length over the limit is refused with too-large before any byte is read, and the stream is cancelled
without Content-Length, bytes are counted while streaming and the stream is cancelled at the limit with too-large (413 over HTTP)
the type is detected from magic bytes (png, jpeg, gif, webp, pdf, zip) and a UTF-8 text heuristic; svg and html markup is recognized
only allowlisted types are stored, and the detected type must agree with the extension and the declared Content-Type
svg and html are refused by default, also when renamed to .txt, and need allowActiveContent to be allowlisted
file names are sanitized (traversal, control and bidi characters, Windows reserved names, byte cap) and bytes are stored under a random key
preflight on File-like objects refuses empty, oversized, unlisted, mismatched and badly named files before upload
authorize gates upload, read and delete per tenant; another tenant's file reads as not found
concurrent uploads cannot exceed the tenant quota (memory store and PGlite), and failed uploads release their reservation
uploads start quarantined; only scanner-clean files are served; infected bytes are deleted and their quota released once
a failing or vague scanner leaves files quarantined; without a scanner nothing is served
downloads carry Content-Disposition attachment with an RFC 6266 filename*, nosniff, the stored detected type and CSP default-src 'none'; sandbox
HTTP adapter: 201 upload, 400, 401, 403 origin and tenant, 404, 405, 409 quarantined, 413, 415 and 204 delete
schema.sql applies and the SQL store keeps conditional status changes and deletes on PostgreSQL
only < followed by a letter, !, ? or / counts as markup; text such as "<3" is plain text
policy.extensions narrows the extensions a type accepts on the server and in preflight, and an extension may belong to one allowed type
filenameControls remove deletes control characters; invalidFilenames reject refuses reserved, empty and dot-only names with invalid-name (400) before the type check and in preflight
checkDeclaredType false ignores the declared Content-Type; lengthMismatch too-large answers a body longer than its Content-Length with too-large
without Content-Length, quota is reserved as bytes arrive, so an upload that fits the remaining quota is accepted (memory store and PGlite)

overlapping scanPending passes and concurrent scan(id) calls run the scanner once per file; a failed scan is retried on the next pass; an abandoned claim expires after scanLeaseMs (memory store and PGlite)

changes: Breaking: UploadMetadataStore adds claimScan, releaseScanClaim and listQuarantined, and schema.sql adds file_uploads.scan_claimed_until (ALTER TABLE file_uploads ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS scan_claimed_until bigint).
Fix: overlapping scan workers could scan one file twice; scans now claim the file, and scanPending() scans every quarantined file for a background job.
Fix: without Content-Length the whole maxBytes was reserved, refusing uploads that fit the remaining quota; quota is now reserved as bytes arrive when maxBytes does not fit.
Fix: text starting with "<" not followed by a letter, !, ? or / ("<3") was refused as html.

New options with the 0.1.0 behavior as default: policy.extensions, policy.filenameControls, policy.invalidFilenames (error code invalid-name), checkDeclaredType, lengthMismatch and scanLeaseMs; sanitizeFilename also takes an options object.
First release: policy and sniffing, browser preflight, core, in-memory stores, PostgreSQL schema and store, and Fetch adapter.
